chunks: A group of scholars narrated to us from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, who said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Aswad (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me, saying: I used to carry the funds that were collected in the office of the endowment to Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari (may Allah have mercy on him), and he would take them from me.
One day, I brought him some of the funds during his last days, two or three years before his death. He ordered me to deliver them to Abul-Qasim al-Ruhi (may Allah be pleased with him).

I would ask him for a receipt, so he complained about that to Abu Ja'far (may Allah be pleased with him). He ordered me not to ask for a receipt, saying: 'Everything that reaches Abul-Qasim has reached me.' After that, I would bring the funds to him and not ask for a receipt.

key_terms.أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ الرُّوحِيُّ: Abul-Qasim al-Ruhi, a deputy of the Imam

ai.seo_question: How did the Imam establish the authority of his deputy over financial endowments during the Minor Occultation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* illustrates the operational mechanics of the *Niyabat al-Aam* (General Deputation) during the Minor Occultation, specifically highlighting the financial autonomy of the deputies. By instructing the narrator to cease demanding formal receipts from Abul-Qasim al-Ruhi, Imam Muhammad ibn Uthman established the principle of *Qabd al-Mutlaq* (absolute possession), where the deputy’s receipt is legally sufficient as the Imam’s own, streamlining administrative efficiency. This narrative underscores the trust placed in the four deputies and serves as a foundational precedent for the validity of their independent financial management in Shia jurisprudence.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 338 - A group of scholars narrated to us from Abu Ja’far Muhammad Ibn Ali Ibn Husain Ibn Babawayh, saying Abu Ja’far Muhammad Ibn Ali Aswad said: I used to carry religious dues procured as endowments to Abu Ja’far Muhammad Ibn Uthman Amari, which he would take from me.
One day, I took some money to him. It was during his last days, two or three years prior to his demise. He ordered me to give them to Abul Qasim Ruh (a.s).

I always asked Abul Qasim for receipts, so he complained to Abu Ja’far about it, and he ordered me, “Don’t insist on receipts and everything that reaches Abul Qasim is as if it reaches me.” After that, I took the dues to him and would not ask for receipts.
